summary: The Gram matrix is an explicit matrix H(N, 0) over O, whose inverse is H(0, N).

steps.claim: A string index c equals s − 1 − c iff s is odd and c = ⌊s/2⌋ (the middle index).
steps.lean: have (c : Fin s) : c = c.rev ↔ if _ : Odd s then c = ⟨s / 2, by grind⟩ else False := by grind
steps.typed_fact: c = c.rev ↔ if _ : Odd s then c = ⟨s / 2, by grind⟩ else False

steps.claim: Let v = e(pt), the last basis vector of X ⊔ {pt}.
Let H(p, q) = gradedGram(e, p) plus, for the middle index b (if any), (q − 1) at (v, v) and −1 at (v, e(b)) and (e(b), v).
steps.lean:
let H (p q : O) := gradedGram e p + ∑ b, ite (b = b.rev)
    (.single v v (q - 1) - .single v (e (.inr b)) 1 - .single (e (.inr b)) v 1) 0

steps.claim: The Gram matrix equals f(H(N, 0)) (using π·π̄ = f(N) and uū = 1), it is hermitian, and H(N, 0)·H(0, N) = 1, so it lies in GL_ι(O); both are checked entrywise, separately for s odd and even.
steps.lean:
refine Eq.subst ?_ ⟨?_, _, ⟨.mkOfMulEqOne (H N 0) (H 0 N) ?_, rfl⟩, rfl⟩ <;> by_cases Odd s <;>
    simp [H, v, *, reindex_equiv e, ← e.sum_comp, apply_ite star,
    apply_ite Subtype.val] <;> grind [star_mul, star_one, Units.mul_inv, u.2.1, map_natCast]
